question.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{2{x}^{4}+3{x}^{3}}{16{x}^{4}-1}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

In this case, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{4}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{4},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{2{x}^{4}+3{x}^{3}}{16{x}^{4}-1} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{3{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{16{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{(2+\frac{3}{x})}{(16-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{3}{x}$ and $\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(2+\frac{3}{x})}{(16-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & \to \frac{2+0}{16-0} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=\frac{1}{8}.$
